title: From Topology to Retrieval: Decoding Embedding Spaces with Unified Signatures
claim: One unified signature vector built from many topological descriptors serves prediction, similarity measurement, and local bias detection.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; global panel stacks two tasks, local panel shows clustering
description: The figure has two gray-headed panels. The left panel, titled 'Global Unified Topological Signatures', lists three embedding-space scatter plots in green, blue and salmon. Each has a colored strip of signature cells beneath it. Two rounded boxes sit to the right. The top box, 'Topology-informed predictions', feeds the stacked signature rows through a 'Model' funnel into a scatter plot with a diagonal fit line. The bottom box, 'Interpretable representational similarity', pairs two signature strips with vertical arrows. It sits beside a summation formula of absolute differences between signature components. The right panel, 'Local Unified Topological Signatures', shows a large point cloud with two circled points linked by dashed lines to grayscale signature strips labeled high and low retrievability. Curved arrows lead to a 'Signature space' UMAP in which green and dark clusters separate.
caption: Unified Topological Signatures of embedding spaces. Left: We construct signature vectors for embedding spaces by computing various topological descriptors. We use the vectors for downstream prediction tasks as well as for measuring representational similarity. Right: We compute local signatures based on the neighborhood of individual embeddings and use them to detect retrievability bias in document corpora.
abstract: Studying the shape of text embedding spaces enhances our understanding of model behavior and how geometry affects downstream task performance. While a range of topological and geometric metrics have been explored, they are typically analyzed in isolation, and the connections between them remain largely unknown. In this paper, we present Unified Topological Signatures (UTS) for characterizing the structure of embedding spaces. We evaluate our method across a wide range of text embedding models and retrieval datasets, finding that it outperforms individual metrics in downstream performance prediction. Through several experiments, we demonstrate that the signatures characterize embedding spaces more accurately, improve the prediction of model-specific properties and biases, and reveal novel insights into representational similarity that challenge the global claims of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis.
